sentences.text: Welcome back to my podcast, English for Everyday Life with Emily.
Today, we are learning how to speak English at a bus terminal.
Taking a bus can be easy, but what if you are in an English -speaking country and don't know how to communicate?
Don't worry.

After this episode, you will know how to buy a bus ticket, ask for bus schedules, find your platform and gate, ask for directions, talk to the bus driver, handle common travel problems, understand bus terminal announcements, stay safe while traveling.
This episode is for A1 -level English learners, so don't worry if you are just starting.
I will speak slowly and clearly and I will explain everything step by step.
Buying a bus ticket.
The first thing you need to do at a bus terminal is buy a ticket.
You can buy a ticket from the ticket counter or use a ticket machine.
Common phrases for buying a ticket.
Hello, I'd like to buy a ticket to New York.
How much is a ticket to Boston?
Do you have a return ticket?
Can I buy a ticket for tomorrow?
Can I pay with cash or card?
Is there a student discount?
Example dialogue.
Hello, I'd like to buy a ticket to Los Angeles, please.
Sure.
One way or return?
One way, please.
How much is it?
That will be $20.
Can I pay with my credit card?
Yes, of course.
Here's your ticket.
The bus leaves at 3 p.m.
from platform 7.
Thank you so much.
Tip if you need a round -trip ticket.
Say, I need a return ticket.
Two, asking for bus schedules.
If you are not sure when your bus leaves, you need to ask about the schedule.
Common phrases for asking schedules.
What time is the next bus to Chicago?
Is there a bus in the evening?
How long is the journey?
What time does the last bus leave?
Example dialogue.
Excuse me, what time is the next bus to Miami?
The next bus leaves at 4.30 p.m.
How long is the journey?
About 6 hours.
Tip, some buses have express routes that are faster.
You can ask, is this an express bus?
Asking for directions at the bus terminal.
Bus stations can be big and confusing.
You may need to ask for directions.
Common phrases for asking directions.
Excuse me, where is platform 5?
Where is the ticket office?
Where are the restrooms?
Which way to the waiting area?
Excuse me, where is platform 12?
It's on the left past the coffee shop.
Thank you so much.
Tip, if you are lost, you can say, I don't know where to go.
Can you help me?
Finding your bus.
Common phrases for finding your bus.
Has the bus to Dallas arrived?
Is this the bus to Toronto?
Where do I board the bus?
Example dialogue.
Excuse me, is this the bus to San Francisco?
Yes, it is.
Do you have your ticket?
Yes, here it is.
Great, you can take a seat.
Tip, always double check before getting on a bus.
Hand of five, understanding bus terminal announcements.
Sometimes you will hear announcements in the bus terminal.
Here are some common announcements.
Attention passengers, the bus to Boston is delayed by 30 minutes.
Final call for the bus to Chicago at platform 10.
The 5 p.m.
bus to Miami is now boarding at gate 4.
Tip, listen carefully to announcements so you don't miss your bus.
Talking to the bus driver.
Common phrases for talking to the driver.
Does this bus stop in Philadelphia?
Where do I get off for the airport?
Can I put my bag in the luggage area?
Example dialogue.
Excuse me, does this bus stop in Houston?
Yes, at the main station.
Thank you.
Handling common travel problems.
If you miss your bus, I miss my bus.
Can I take the next one?
If your ticket is lost, I lost my ticket.
What should I do?
If you are at the wrong station, is this the main bus station?
Example dialogue.
I miss my bus.
Can I take the next one?
Ticket agent.
Yes, but there is a small fee.
Tip, always check your ticket carefully.
Final tips for speaking English at a bus terminal.
Arrive early so you don't miss your bus.
Keep your ticket safe in your bag or pocket.
Check the schedule before your trip.
If you are lost, ask for help.
Thank you for listening.
I hope you now feel more confident speaking English at a bus terminal.
If you enjoyed this episode, please subscribe and share it with your friends.
See you next time.
Bye -bye.
